summary.text: A 23-year-old unmarried nulligravida woman presented to the outpatient department with a 2-month history of progressive abdominal fullness, discomfort, irregular menses and early satiety. She had no pertinent medical, surgical or family history of ovarian tumor, and examination showed a large firm mobile nontender abdominal mass equivalent to a 34 week gestation.

Ultrasonography and contrast-enhanced CT showed a large multiloculated right adnexal cystic lesion with septations and an enhancing solid component, suggestive of mucinous cystadenoma. CA-125 was 306.9 U/mL. Laparotomy found a huge right ovarian cyst, imprint cytology indicated borderline malignancy, and staging surgery was performed.

Final histopathology reported stage IA, grade 1, well differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma of the ovary with strong CK7 and CK20 positivity and PAS positivity. After counseling, and given her unmarried status and wish for future childbearing, the patient and family opted for completion surgery two weeks after the histopathology report, which included hysterectomy and left salpingo-oophorectomy; repeat peritoneal fluid cytology was positive for malignant cells.

Because of malignant cells in the peritoneal fluid she was referred to clinical oncology and received 6 cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel. She remains on three-monthly follow-up with normal tumor markers and ultrasonography and is doing well without evidence of recurrence one year after surgery.
